sources.title: A bunch of Grand Theft Auto games will be cheap on Steam until GTA 6 comes out, and only one sucks
sources.text: In the run-up to GTA 6 's November 19 launch, Rockstar has multiple classic Grand Theft Auto games on sale on Steam – and, nearest I can tell, only on Steam. The Nintendo Switch eShop actually has a competing deal for the Grand Theft Auto Definitive Edition Trilogy, which is down 67% to $19.79, but that sale ends in 11 hours from the time of writing. On Steam, several GTA games are discounted until November 19 for an obviously timed special promotion. On Steam, you'll find four games on sale via two actual products: You can't argue with GTA 4 for $6, but you might argue with this version of, in particular, GTA 3. The Definitive Edition Trilogy was famously panned at launch for wonky graphics and poor technical performance that, for the most part, has been patched up in the years since. However, the PC port for GTA 3's Definitive Edition is uniquely poorly rated for reasons that will sound familiar. Here's how the three games in this trilogy compare in Steam reviews: The reception to the two other games in the trilogy improved over time while GTA 3 steadily declined. Much like the day-one reviews, today's Steam players complain of Rockstar launcher interference, bugs, shoddy art, broken cinematics, and performance dips. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Curiously, perhaps unrelated to the quality of the port, some of today's gamers also don't seem to take too kindly to GTA 3's design sensibilities, it being slightly older than Vice City and San Andreas, and certainly a rawer open-world experience. Thomas Williamson, the CEO of the outsourced trilogy's original developer, Grove Street Games, said earlier this year that the criticism faced at launch was deserved. "I agreed with most of the people's reactions," he said. "But unfortunately, I feel like we did not agree with how the game was released and the response to it from a development side. And I think that would have changed the narrative significantly." However, he added, "at the end of the day, looking at the behind-the-scenes metrics on those games, there were a lot of people who were playing them and really enjoying them." You won't find Grove Street Games listed on the store pages for these games anymore. Previously, Williamson called it a "dick move" for Rockstar to have Grove Street's name removed. GTA 6 being pirated is just "a fact of life," says CEO of Rockstar owner, and lawyers are ready if it becomes a problem Austin has been a game journalist for 12 years, having freelanced for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, IGN, Sports Illustrated, and more while finishing his journalism degree. He's been with GamesRadar+ since 2019. They've yet to realize his position is a cover for his career-spanning Destiny column, and he's kept the ruse going with a lot of news and the occasional feature, all while playing as many roguelikes as possible. sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Rockstar's having a sale on old GTA games on the only platform Grand Theft Auto 6 isn't coming to (ours)
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 finally arrives on November 19, but not for us, no—the big day is only for gamers on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. We're not being completely excluded, though: We can't have GTA 6 in November, but we can take advantage of pre-release discounts on a bunch of older GTA games—deals that, ironically, don't appear to be available on consoles. As noted by GamesRadar , there are four GTA games available in two releases: Grand Theft Auto 3, Vice City, and San Andreas bundled up in the GTA Trilogy for $19.79/£19.79/€19.79—67% off the regular price—and Grand Theft Auto 4: Complete Edition , which includes The Lost and Damned and The Ballad of Gay Tony expansions, for $6/£5.09/€6, a 70% discount. Those aren't the deepest discounts ever seen, but Grand Theft Auto games typically don't venture into the 90% off territory we all enjoy so much—and according to Isthereanydeal.com, this is as low as the GTA Trilogy has ever gone, and close to the mark for GTA 4 . You may recall that the GTA Trilogy Definitive Edition was a mess when it launched in 2021, but it seems to have turned that frown upside-down since then: On Steam, where the trilogy arrived in 2023, Vice City and San Andreas both hold "very positive" ratings. GTA 3 is stuck at a "mixed" rating, which is unfortunate: Glancing at user reviews, it sounds like the game still isn't in perfect shape, but it's also suffering from the fact that it's 25 years old, and was the first 3D game in the series—some jank and roughness was there right from the start. Grand Theft Auto 4: The Complete Edition, on the other hand, doesn't suffer from those shortcomings. It's getting pretty long in the tooth too—it came out in 2008—but represents a shift in design and tone that led the series into what it is today. If you're looking for just one older GTA game to horse around with, this is the one, especially given that it's less than half the cost of the trilogy. As mentioned, these sale prices are currently only being offered on Steam: There's currently no sign of any of them on either the Xbox or PlayStation stores (Fun fact: there actually is no digital version of GTA 4 on the PS Store because Sony didn't start selling full-priced games online until well after 2008). Maybe it's just coincidence, but they do appear to be intentional pre-GTA 6 sales: The discounts are on until November 19, when Grand Theft Auto 6 launches—except on PC. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Will Have 55 Trophies/Achievements
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 is set to be a completionist’s dream. It has been racking up more side content promises than any game to come in the series thus far; there are indications it’s the longest single-player campaign in franchise history, and the world is absolutely gargantuan. That means we can expect a substantial array of GTA 6 Trophies and Achievements to surface, depending on your platform of choice. In fact, thanks to a recent comment on social media, we know how many are coming, and it’s more than Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA 5 had at launch. Rockstar Games is all about the ultimate immersion in Grand Theft Auto 6. As they said in a recent interview, they want you to live a life inside GTA 6, which is set to drop in just 11 days, on November 19th. It’s likely the densest Grand Theft Auto title ever made . While you’re immersed, you’ll be able to chase a thick assortment of Trophies and Achievements. The former if you’re on PlayStation, and the latter if you’re an XBOX player, of course. What’s interesting is that Grand Theft Auto 6, with 55 Trophies/Achievements , beats both Grand Theft Auto 5 (51) and Red Dead Redemption 2 (52). It’s not a huge edge, but it’s an edge nonetheless. It’s also worth pointing out that GTA 5 eventually went on to get 78 Trophies/Achievements with the addition of GTA Online content over the years, so there’s every opportunity for GTA 6 to do the same thing. Hell, perhaps this will be the first Grand Theft Auto 6 title to get a single-player expansion since GTA 4. If you want to go the whole hog and 100% Grand Theft Auto 6, you’ll be pleased to know that data suggests there are both a Platinum Trophy and a Mythic Achievement. The latter is the new tier that XBOX put in place in recognition of players who have gone the distance with their games. Grand Theft Auto 6 launches November 19th on XBOX Series X|S and PlayStation 5, and pre-loading will start globally on November 10th. Are you looking forward to GTA 6? sources.text: O Xbox Game Pass é um dos serviços de assinatura de games mais democráticos da atualidade, já que é possível acessá-lo de diferentes plataformas — incluindo os próprios, consoles da Microsoft, assim como no PC, nuvem, celulares, tablets e até Smart TVs Samsung e LG com modelos de 2022 para cá. Felizmente, seu catálogo também é atualizado quase que semanalmente, trazendo inúmeras opções para os assinantes aproveitarem — e o melhor de tudo: gastando pouco em comparação às novas tendências de preços da indústria. Se veio em busca de novos jogos para jogar através do Xbox Game Pass , está no lugar certo. O serviço ganhou um reforço de peso esta semana com a chegada de seis títulos para os assinantes aproveitarem. Confira abaixo mais informações sobre as novas aventuras! Em Pit of Goblin os jogadores assumem o papel de goblins que precisam explorar masmorras, escapar de armadilhas e fugir de monstros para alimentar o Rei-Rainha Goblin. O jogo aposta no terror cooperativo online, permitindo formar equipes com amigos ou encarar os desafios sozinho. Mas cuidado: se a missão falhar, você pode acabar virando a próxima refeição! Dos mesmos criadores de Vampire Survivors , Vampire Crawlers: The Turbo Wildcard from Vampire Survivors transforma a fórmula de ação do original em uma aventura de exploração de masmorras em primeira pessoa. Com elementos de roguelite e combate por turnos, o game permite montar baralhos de cartas e criar combinações poderosas para enfrentar inimigos e explorar cenários conhecidos da franquia. Void/Breaker é um FPS roguelite em que os jogadores precisam escapar de um ciclo interminável controlado por uma inteligência artificial hostil. Disponível na versão 1.0 para Xbox Series X|S e Cloud Gaming, o jogo traz combates contra máquinas, além de um sistema de modificações que permite criar diferentes combinações de armas e habilidades. Disponível no lançamento pelo Xbox Game Pass, Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School aposta em uma nova abordagem para os jogos de escape room ao apresentar um mundo aberto repleto de enigmas. A aventura pode ser aproveitada em modo cooperativo local ou online para dois jogadores, que precisam trabalhar juntos para solucionar desafios e escapar das salas. Em Firefighting Simulator: Ignite , os jogadores assumem o papel de bombeiros nos Estados Unidos e precisam enfrentar incêndios, lidar com situações de risco e salvar vidas. O simulador permite formar equipes com até três amigos no modo cooperativo ou contar com personagens controlados pela inteligência artificial para auxiliar nas operações. Por fim, MySims Cozy Bundle reúne versões retrabalhadas de dois jogos da franquia: MySims e MySims Kingdom . Os jogadores podem personalizar uma cidade, explorar um reino de fantasia, fazer amizades e participar de diferentes atividades, incluindo a resolução de quebra-cabeças e a construção e decoração de ambientes. O pacote está disponível nos consoles e no Cloud Gaming. Curtiu as indicações para jogar no Xbox Game Pass? Vale a pena dar uma conferida em Void/Breaker , hein? sources.text: MARVEL Cosmic Invasion ’s Castle Doom mode gets extended gameplay ahead of its November 10 DLC launch, with branching paths and 12 perks. At launch, the roster included Wolverine, Spider-Man, Venom, Captain America, and Iron Man. The game initially launched in December 2025 and has since accumulated over 2 million players. In addition to the new game mode mentioned above, this next DLC pack will include new characters. The playable characters are Doctor Doom and The Invisible Woman. sources.title: After furloughing its developers and then hiring some of them back, Star Wars Zero Company developer has laid off an unspecified number of staff
sources.text: "While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together." Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has laid of an unspecified number of developers, after furloughing its entire team and then hiring some of that staff back. As reported by the Star Wars website Bespin Bulletin, several designers of the acclaimed tactics game have taken to LinkedIn to announce that they have been let go by the studio. Among those affected are senior environment artist Ryan Lopez, who worked on the game for three and a half years and has been on furlough for the past three and a half months. "While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together," Lopez wrote in a LinkedIn post . Other designers who lost their jobs include UI Engineer Tyler Eichten and senior quality assurance analyst Ryan Mosher , who spent two years at Firaxis and a further two years at 1047 Games before joining Bit Reactor in October 2024. It's been a tumultuous few months for Bit Reactor. In September, it was reported that the studio had furloughed up to 80% of its staff in the weeks leading up to Zero Company's launch, with the studio having reportedly "run out of most of its money" ahead of the game's launch. At the time, former senior technical artist Zachariah Scott said the project was built with "shocking austerity". Scott also accused Bit Reactor of "concealing the fact that the team was furloughed weeks ago" after the company made the announcement. Within a month, Zero Company had sold one million copies and Bit Reactor subsequently announced it had hired back some of its staff. In a statement posted on Bluesky, CEO Greg Foertsch stated that the furlough had been a response to "unexpected business developments outside of our control" and "necessary to help us eventually bring as many people back as we can". Clearly, though, Zero Company's commercial performance hasn't been enough to bring back everybody. Which is a shame, considering that Zero Company is by all accounts a brilliant Star Wars adventure. Resident word Jedi Ted Litchfield called it "one of the best games of 2026 and a new all-timer Star Wars videogame" in his Star Wars Zero Company Review . Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. Zero Company isn't the only knockout Star Wars game to release this year either, with Star Wars: Galactic Racer providing a similarly scintillating experience in a galaxy far, far away. Indeed, the performance of both games appears to have pleased Star Wars overlords Lucasfilm, and the company is keen to do more creative spins on the universe in the vein of Zero Company and Galactic Racer. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex. Between 2013 and 2022, Rick was games editor of Custom PC magazine and associated website bit-tech.net . But he's always kept one foot in freelance games journalism, writing for publications like Edge, Eurogamer, the Guardian and, naturally, PC Gamer. While he'll play anything that can be controlled with a keyboard and mouse, he has a particular passion for first-person shooters and immersive sims. sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Star Wars Zero Company studio Bit Reactor lays off staff, a month after bringing furloughed developers back
sources.text: "While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together." Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has laid off an unspecified number of staff, a month after bringing some of its furloughed team back to work. Several developers announced on LinkedIn on Friday, 6th November, that they had been let go, as first reported by Bespin Bulletin . Bit Reactor hasn't said how many people are affected. Among them is senior environment artist Ryan Lopez, who spent three and a half years working on Zero Company, from pre-production to launch, and was laid off after a three-month furlough. UI engineer Tyler Eichten, who worked on much of the on-screen UI for the game's tactical missions, and Ryan Mosher from the QA team have also confirmed they were let go. "While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together," Lopez wrote . "It was a privilege to ship a game with you." Bit Reactor furloughed most of its staff in the weeks before Zero Company launched on 27th August, with one source putting the figure at roughly 80 percent. The studio appeared to have run out of money just short of release. The game did well regardless, and is thought to have sold more than a million copies within a month . Then, in a message shared on Bluesky on 7th October, CEO Greg Foertsch said the studio had "started the process of returning more of our team back to work". Asking staff to step away so close to launch was "an incredibly difficult decision", he said, "but one that was necessary to help us eventually bring as many people back as possible". It's thought more than half the studio returned, though not everyone went back on full pay. It's not clear whether any of those who returned were among the people laid off this week. In Eurogamer's Star Wars Zero Company review , we awarded the game four out of five stars, saying, "an already winning genre is matched with the perfect setting in this earnest, heartfelt, smart and slightly ramshackle turn-based tactics gem".

stories.title: Sony Indefinitely Delays Another PlayStation Accessory Just A Week Before Launch
stories.summary: Sony cites a 'production issue' as hardware shortages stymie what would have been an otherwise whirlwind holiday season for the console

sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: Sony Indefinitely Delays Another PlayStation Accessory Just A Week Before Launch
sources.text: Hardware PlayStation 5 PlayStation Portal Sony One year ago, during PlayStationâs 2025 State of Play , Sony announced their Pulse Elevate speakers. A set of two, wireless gaming-focused speakers for the home console and desktop experience alike. Complementing their in-house line of earbuds, the speakers were to hit shelves this Thursday. With days to go, Sony updated the Pulseâs announcement page to say that they have been delayed. “As part of our ongoing quality testing of Pulse Elevate speakers, we have identified a production issue with the product and have made the decision to delay the launch,” reads the update . “The additional time will allow us to ensure the product will deliver the experience we intended for our players. We apologize for the delay and appreciate your patience and understanding. We look forward to bringing Pulse Elevate to players soon.” Similar to the Pulse brand of earbuds, the Pulse Elevate speakers were designed with the PlayStation 5 and Portal in mind, but could pair with PC, Mac and even mobile gaming experiences. The product promised to blast 3D audio from compatible PlayStation games and a built-in mic with AI-powered noise reduction. The original release date was November 12th, with pre-orders opening in September and hardware influencers seemingly receiving their copies . No new timeline, release date or refund policy has been announced from this delay. Sony pulled a similar move with the FlexStrike Wireless Fight Stick that was supposed to arrive alongside Marvel Token: Fighting Souls . The accessory was delayed in July and still hasn’t shipped or even received an updated release date. With Grand Theft Auto VI just a few blocks away, and the PlayStation the primary console to play it on, this should be an exceptionally stellar holiday season for Sony. Instead, between trade wars, component shortages, rising costs and AI RAM hoarding , Sony seems unable to keep up with demand . Just last week the company unveiled an unusual buyback program , an effort to keep these gizmos circulating amid difficult stock. What exactly spurred the Pulse delay is unspecified. Sony was traditionally a consumer tech, home entertainment focused company, so this isnât their first rodeo. In recent years, however, the company has seemingly drifted towards producing the media consumed on television instead of the television itself, following years of more affordable options in the industry. This is made most clear in their decision to abandon physical discs, printing that propriety format being the reason PlayStation exists in the first place . sources.title: Sony delays PlayStation's Pulse Elevate speakers indefinitely, less than a week before launch
sources.text: Sony has delayed its Pulse Elevate wireless speakers indefinitely, less than a week before they were due to launch. The news came in a 6th November update to Sony’s original announcement on the PlayStation Blog , first spotted by IGN . Quality testing has turned up a "production issue", Sony said, and there's no new release date yet. "As part of our ongoing quality testing of Pulse Elevate speakers, we have identified a production issue with the product and have made the decision to delay the launch," the statement reads. "The additional time will allow us to ensure the product will deliver the experience we intended for our players. We apologise for the delay and appreciate your patience and understanding. We look forward to bringing Pulse Elevate to players soon." The speakers were set to go on sale worldwide on 12th November, and pre-orders opened in September. It's unclear what, exactly, happens to those orders, but we'll update as and when we find out more. Sony revealed Pulse Elevate in September 2025 as its first wireless speakers for desktop gaming. They sit alongside the Pulse Elite headset and Pulse Explore earbuds, and cost £199.99 ($219.99). They connect to PS5, PC, Mac, and PlayStation Portal via PlayStation Link, and can pair with a phone over Bluetooth at the same time. There's also a microphone in the right speaker with what Sony calls "AI-enhanced noise rejection". Midnight Black was due to be available everywhere, while the White version was limited to a handful of countries, including the UK. Alongside the Pulse Elevate speakers, Sony revealed a range of hardware in September 2025, including a 27-inch gaming monitor that's coming only to the US and Japan .

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: BioWare May Be Dead, But a Modder Has Rebuilt Mass Effect 3's Multiplayer Into the Legendary Edition
sources.text: When the Mass Effect Legendary Edition came out in 2021, it included the single player campaign of all three original games, along with all the DLC. But while all the story content you could ever want was included, Mass Effect 3's multiplayer mode was conspicuously absent, despite having a dedicated fanbase. Now, just a few weeks after EA's shutdown of BioWare , a team of modders has successfully ported Mass Effect 3 's multiplayer to the Legendary Edition, with all the graphics and engine improvements that came with that re-release. The mod will be coming out on N7 Day – November 7th – and will be free to play, as long as you already own Mass Effect Legendary Edition. I also got a chance to sit down with Mgamerz, who runs the ME3Tweaks team that created the mod, to talk about Mass Effect 3, and about the state of modding in 2026. And if you want to download the mod yourself, it's available now on Nexus Mods. IGN: So, tell me a little bit about the project, and how you got started on basically porting the Mass Effect 3 multiplayer over to the Legendary Edition. Mgamerz: Yeah, so my dev team, ME3Tweaks, and I run it. We ported Pinnacle Station back in 2021. Crazy effort. I don't know how we got that done in a two-month timeframe. And then we were doing other projects for two years, and then near the end of me working on LE2 Randomizer, which is a randomizer for legendary Mass Effect 2, someone discovered a copy of the Citadel in Mass Effect 2. There's an area from the wards. I can't remember which game it was, but they found an area of the game that nobody knew about before, and you could load into and you're like, 'Well, this was clearly supposed to be something, and then they just never finished it.' It was a very early prototype. And it was like, 'Man, what if we could port something like that into another level?' And so I made this project called Project Wardle, Ward being the first part of it. (We have a bunch of stupid internal code names.) And I eventually made it so we could port a Mass Effect 2 level into Mass Effect 3, and we fixed up the cover, because cover is just an unbelievable nightmare. It's very important for enemies to be able to use it. Gameplay's a huge component of why Mass Effect 3 is fun. And we got that working and then I was like, 'Well, man, what if we could port the multiplayer levels?' Because we did it for Pinnacle Station. We ported the old game. But Pinnacle Station is mostly just reused assets from Mass Effect 1. Like 90% of it was just existing assets that they just reused. But multiplayer was totally different. It's like, yeah, none of this content exists. So the scope of work is just huge. So at the end of 2023, right as we finished LE2 Randomizer, literally on N7 day, I spun up a new Discord. I invited a couple people and they're like, 'What's this Discord about?' I'm like, 'We're going to do something stupid. We're going to port [Mass Effect 3] Multiplayer.' And those were the first two messages I ever sent. I have some screenshots of it. And then people were like, 'Yeah, you're joking, right?' And I'm like, 'No.' And then the last three years we've been working on it. It hasn't been constant. Last year I broke my arm, which set us back six to eight months. But for the first two years, it was tons of prototyping. Within the first month of this project, we actually had multiplayer working. It was a proof of concept. And then we spent the next two years getting audio to port, from a different version of the audio engine because they upgraded it. It's like we got shaders building, which was a total nightmare because BioWare compiled the game with a bunch of sources that don't ship with the game. And so we had to figure out 'how do we replicate that?' So that took a long time. And then it's like textures. We have a bunch more people that know how to do texture upscaling. The first two years is almost all prototype and then asset generation. We want to make it look good. We're planning stuff out, that kind of stuff. So that's really not how it started. IGN: So, you basically built from scratch again? Did you take assets from the original Mass Effect 3? Mgamerz: Oh yeah, the whole thing ports from it. It's not a one-to-one port. We're not just taking Mass Effect 3 multiplayer and dumping it into Legendary Edition and then, 'Hey guys, check out it's multiplayer, [as] you remember it.' Where we took a lot of extra steps, the lighting actually gets re-baked in Unreal Engine 4's light solver. Essentially what that means is, imagine you have a light bulb in a room and if you wanted to project what the lights would look like, a light beam's going to hit your microphone and it's going to cast a shadow. And then that light bounces off for you, goes into your closet and it bounces off and illuminates the closet a little bit from the inside. Unreal Engine 3 had a solver and that's how all of the lighting for all the Unreal Engine 3 games worked. But in Unreal Engine 4, they added like, 'Oh, we can do additional light bounces or we found a better statistical way to do light bounces.' And so you get crisper shadow edges or the more soft, like a grate covering on some maps. The light bounces through the grate, and unless you have super high resolution textures, it looks terrible. Mass Effect 3 is full of terrible light maps. If you look at them, you're like, 'Wow, it's just a big stair step of shadows and it looks bad.' And so we spent a lot of time upgrading that kind of stuff. I modded Mass Effect 3 multiplayer for eight years before Legendary Edition came out, and there's a bunch of stuff I was like, 'Wow, I didn't even realize three of the character classes don't even use the highest-quality mesh.' So it's like BioWare made the Geth Infiltrator, and they made it at a high quality where it has all the polygons and triangles. And then as you get further away from the camera, it gets less triangles, because you can't see as much detail. But BioWare was just like, 'We'r

sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: How Modders Spent Three Years Remastering Mass Effect 3’s Fantastic Multiplayer For Legendary Edition: ‘Let’s Do Something Stupid’
sources.text: Mass Effect 3 Mass Effect: Legendary Edition Mass Effect: Universe N7 Day When the Mass Effect: Legendary Edition remasters launched in 2021, they had just about everything you could have wanted from a modern-day port of BioWareâs sci-fi RPGs. There were, however, two major exemptions: the original gameâs Pinnacle Station DLC , and Mass Effect 3 âs cooperative multiplayer mode. In 2021, the ME3Tweaks modding group brought back Pinnacle Station . Now, five years later, itâs back to finish the job, and is releasing a remastered mod of the multiplayer mode for those who have the Legendary Edition on PC. The project began in earnest three years ago, with modder Mgamerz coming up with the idea shortly after wrapping up a randomizer mod for the Mass Effect 2 remaster. Luckily, the ME3Tweaks group had a lot of the foundations set in place to bring the missing mode into the Legendary Edition after years of working in the Mass Effect modding space. âThere was somebody who had shown that they could port a level when they found an unused level in [ Mass Effect 1 âs remaster],â he tells Kotaku . âThere was like an extra Citadel area, and I was like, âOh man, what if I could port that to another game?â Sometimes I just get these crazy ideas, like, âWhat if I just did something crazy?â And so I tried porting it, and I was able to actually get it to port because we did Pinnacle Station , so we had a lot of the infrastructure to do it, and I was able to port it. I’m like, âman, what if we could do like a multiplayer level?â And I was able to port, I think it was [Firebase] Condor. It’s one of the first DLC maps. ItÂ looked terrible, but you didn’t immediately crash the game loading into it. And I had already ported multiplayer levels before in my Redemption map pack that I had made from single player to multiplayer, so I kind of knew everything that was needed. And then it was like, âOkay, well, I made this map, but there’s no game mode; you can’t do anything on it. Really, it looks terrible.â And so I kind of shelved it for a couple of months.â After some time, Mgamerz decided he wanted to make a multiplayer mod, and thus went back to the original Mass Effect 3 , and says he was struck by how much âfurther advancedâ the groupâs modding tools had become while working on the remaster.Â âLiterally probably about three hours into it, I’m like, âThese tools suck,â and I say that as someone who helped write most of them. Our tooling for the original trilogy is so bad compared to what we got in Legendary Edition .â Part of that is because, prior to the remasterâs launch, the ME3Tweaks group had meetings with folks at BioWare about making the Legendary Edition more modder-friendly, and although the company wasnât able to implement everything, it did give the group a better starting point. âIt was probably just like a month before the game release,â he recalls. âWe gave them a list of some of the most awful things we have to deal with, and we kind of didn’t expect them to do most of the changes. And they didn’t. I mean, it’s one month before launch, so you can’t really make big changes. But they snuck a few in right at the end of development for us, which has helped a lot of single-player development. They gave us some information that we couldn’t really leverage until we started working on stuff like this, like how does DLC mount work? When the game loads, DLC mounts into the game, but in ME3 , it loads single-player versus multiplayer, and we didn’t really have any idea how any of that worked. So they gave us information about that, and then we, you know, over the years we built on top of it.â Over two years later, on November 7, 2023, Mgamerz created a Discord server for Project Milan, what would become the Mass Effect 3 Legendary Edition multiplayer remaster mod, telling the rest of the ME3Tweaks modders, “Let’s do something stupid. Let’s port multiplayer.” He says that development was on and off over the course of three years, citing some personal matters that got in the way including breaking his arm at some point during the whole effort, but the group had a working prototype of the mode as early as December of 2023.Â “You could pick at least one kit, and the game didn’t crash until you got to wave three,” he recalls. “Enemies would spawn. Audio was totally broken. Like there was virtually no audio. The shaders were all broken, so you just got checkerboards all over the place. But you could actually play it, and enemies spawn. You could kill them. You get points. You know, the absolute bare bones were there.” From there, the team built the rest of the multiplayer mode back up, but it isnât just what BioWare created in 2012, as the mod includes new ways of play, as well as some alterations to the multiplayerâs progression system. What started as a scheme to bring the old multiplayer mode back to the masses became much more as Mgamerz says the team got âtoo ambitiousâ and decided to add more on top of the old bones. This includes new modes Coalition, which pivots between different enemy factions across a match with each wave hosting a different group, and Unified, which mixes enemies from all groups together. âit picks a quasi-random list of enemies,â Mgamerz says. âOriginally we had it fully random, and that was terrible. It was so bad, but now it draws from all of the different wavelist options and picks from those, so you get like a mix of the original compositions that we made, and that one actually is pretty fun.â One notable fact about the multiplayer mode is that it was one of the earliest examples of a game using modern-day loot boxes to let players unlock characters and acquire consumables. stories.title: Assassin's Creed is reportedly going to ancient Rome, while a mobile spin-off heads to Jerusalem
stories.summary: Ubisoft is reportedly working on two new Assassin's Creed games , and one of them is set in ancient Rome. Read more

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Assassin's Creed is reportedly going to ancient Rome, while a mobile spin-off heads to Jerusalem
sources.text: Ubisoft is reportedly working on two new Assassin's Creed games , and one of them is set in ancient Rome. That's according to YouTuber Xj0nathan, who says the Rome game is codenamed Mars. He claims two sources with access to Ubisoft's backend systems backed up the information, and that the setting will likely be linked to the upcoming Assassin's Creed TV series. The second game, codenamed Pocket, is said to be a mobile title set in Jerusalem. Xj0nathan claims it'll play a bit like Assassin’s Creed Valhalla’s Mastery Challenge, and look similar to the most recent Prince of Persia. The hero's mentor is apparently a character called Myriam. Insider Gaming says it's heard the codenames too, but couldn't confirm them well enough to report them independently. It puts some of that down to the turbulence the franchise has gone through since former Assassin's Creed boss Marc-Alexis Côté left Ubisoft. Last month, the outlet's sources also claimed Assassin's Creed Hexe, the next mainline game, had been delayed internally by another year, likely to 2028. Other reports claim we'll see it next year. If Mars does move into full production, don't hold your breath - Insider Gaming doesn't expect us to hear anything about it until 2029 or 2030. Assassin's Creed has visited Rome before, in 2010’s Brotherhood, but that was the Renaissance version of the city. The leak comes less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series , insisting there are currently no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

sources.name: Polygon
sources.title: Assassin's Creed Hexe Reportedly Delayed As New Assassin's Creed Games Leak
sources.text: Some new insider reporting has shed new light on the future of Assassin's Creed Some new reports regarding the Assassin's Creed series emerged last week, giving us a better idea of what to expect from Ubisoft's flagship series for the rest of the decade. While we learned about two Assassin's Creed titles for the first time, it has also been reported that the development of Assassin's Creed Hexe is taking longer than expected. On Nov. 6, Ubisoft insider j0nathan posted a YouTube video in which he teased two new Assassin's Creed games. One is codenamed Mars and is reportedly a traditional Assassin's Creed game set in Ancient Rome, the same era in which the show's upcoming Netflix adaptation is set. The other is Assassin's Creed Pocket , a mobile game inspired by Valhalla's Mastery Challenges that will be set in Jerusalem. Insider Gaming followed up the next day to say that it'd heard of Assassin's Creed games with similar codenames, although it was not able to verify the projects enough to report on them first. It then revealed some more verified information about Assassin's Creed Hexe : While it was expected to be released in 2027, it has internally been pushed back to 2028. Assassin's Creed Hexe was first teased by Ubisoft in 2022 , and is supposed to have a more magical edge and be set in the Holy Roman Empire during the 17th century. While Ubisoft has promised to reveal more about the game next year, we've yet to actually see the game in action. According to Insider Gaming, Hexe's development has "had issues," with several high-level developers exiting Ubisoft during its development. Insider Gaming now does not expect Hexe to launch until 2028; in turn, it also reports that Mars likely wouldn't be released, or even revealed, until 2029 or 2030 at the earliest. For now, we'll just have to stick to playing Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced .
